taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes it is composed of two groups formerly considered separate species, aeneus (Bronzed) and armenti (Bronze-brown, South America), and is often placed in genus Tangavius (AOU 1998).
fieldMarks: Larger than Brown-headed Cowbird, with a longer bill and shorter tail
Red eyes (hard to see); neck ruff gives a hunched-shoulder look
Females dull black in Texas or gray-brown in Arizona
behavior: Only a short-distance migrant; very uncommon and local in the Southwest in winter, some stray east along the Gulf Coast to Florida
Forages mostly walking on the ground in the open, sometimes with cattle or horses; may take ticks or insects from cattle backs
Diet is largely seeds and waste grain, plus insects, snails and spiders; snails may supply calcium to laying females
habitat: Farmland, brush, semi-open country and feedlots; outside breeding generally very open lowland habitats, roosting in brushy woods.
range: Resident from extreme southeastern California, Arizona, southwestern New Mexico and western and southern Texas south to Panama; northern populations partially migratory.
